channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Endgame to Failure: How the Zero-Tolerance Campaign Against Nicotine Will Backfire
item.description: Zero tolerance sounds clean until it meets real life. People do not stop wanting nicotine because policy declares the end of nicotine; they move towards whatever remains available, affordable and believable. That can mean illicit markets, continued smoking or mistrust of public health advice that refuses to distinguish between risk levels. A strategy built on eliminating nicotine may backfire unless it first deals honestly with why safer alternatives exist. (Published on September 24, 2026byc2cjournal.ca)

item.title: Knowledge is Power
item.description: Knowledge is power in tobacco harm reduction because it gives smokers something more useful than fear. Understanding combustion, nicotine, relative risk and switching can change the choices people believe are available to them. Poor information keeps cigarettes protected by confusion, while clear information helps adults see a route away from the most harmful product. Public health should not be afraid of informed consumers; it should depend on them. (Published on September 24, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: France Banned Nicotine Pouches! What Happens Next?
item.description: France has chosen to close the door on nicotine pouches, but the demand they answered will not vanish with the ban. Adult smokers and nicotine users may now be pushed towards cross-border purchases, informal supply or the one product still widely available: cigarettes. That is the weakness of treating smoke-free alternatives as threats instead of regulating them as part of a risk hierarchy. The real test comes next — whether the ban reduces harm, or simply moves it somewhere less visible. (Published on September 24, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Teen Vaping Is Falling in Pennsylvania...so why does the state still say it is skyrocketing
item.description: Pennsylvania’s teen vaping trend tells a less dramatic story than many policy campaigns suggest. Youth use is falling, yet the political response often remains locked in crisis mode, with restrictions aimed at a problem that may already be moving in the right direction. That matters because outdated alarm can distort priorities and spill over onto adults who smoke. Prevention should follow the data, not preserve a panic after the trend has changed. (Published on September 24, 2026bysubstack.com)
